paragraphs.text: Now I Paul myself entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am of good courage toward you:
paragraphs.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐγὼ Παῦλος παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς διὰ τῆς πραΰτητος καὶ ἐπιεικείας τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς κατὰ πρόσωπον μὲν ταπεινὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀπὼν δὲ θαρρῶ εἰς ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: Autos de egō Paulos parakalō hymas dia tēs prautētos kai epieikeias tou Christou, hos kata prosōpon men tapeinos en hymin, apōn de tharrō eis hymas·

paragraphs.text: yea, I beseech you, that I may not when present show courage with the confidence wherewith I count to be bold against some, who count of us as if we walked according to the flesh.
paragraphs.original: δέομαι δὲ τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι τῇ πεποιθήσει ᾗ λογίζομαι τολμῆσαι ἐπί τινας τοὺς λογιζομένους ἡμᾶς ὡς κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦντας.
paragraphs.translit: deomai de to mē parōn tharrēsai tē pepoithēsei hē logizomai tolmēsai epi tinas tous logizomenous hēmas hōs kata sarka peripatountas.

paragraphs.text: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh
paragraphs.original: ἐν σαρκὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦντες οὐ κατὰ σάρκα στρατευόμεθα—
paragraphs.translit: en sarki gar peripatountes ou kata sarka strateuometha—

paragraphs.text: (for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the casting down of strongholds),
paragraphs.original: τὰ γὰρ ὅπλα τῆς στρατείας ἡμῶν οὐ σαρκικὰ ἀλλὰ δυνατὰ τῷ θεῷ πρὸς καθαίρεσιν ὀχυρωμάτων— λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες
paragraphs.translit: ta gar hopla tēs strateias hēmōn ou sarkika alla dynata tō theō pros kathairesin ochyrōmatōn— logismous kathairountes

paragraphs.text: casting down imaginations, and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God, and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ;
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντες πᾶν νόημα εἰς τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai pan hypsōma epairomenon kata tēs gnōseōs tou theou, kai aichmalōtizontes pan noēma eis tēn hypakoēn tou Christou,

paragraphs.text: and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be made full.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες ἐκδικῆσαι πᾶσαν παρακοήν, ὅταν πληρωθῇ ὑμῶν ἡ ὑπακοή.
paragraphs.translit: kai en hetoimō echontes ekdikēsai pasan parakoēn, hotan plērōthē hymōn hē hypakoē.

paragraphs.text: Ye look at the things that are before your face. If any man trusteth in himself that he is Christ`s, let him consider this again with himself, that, even as he is Christ`s, so also are we.
paragraphs.original: Τὰ κατὰ πρόσωπον βλέπετε. εἴ τις πέποιθεν ἑαυτῷ Χριστοῦ εἶναι, τοῦτο λογιζέσθω πάλιν ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῦ ὅτι καθὼς αὐτὸς Χριστοῦ οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Ta kata prosōpon blepete. ei tis pepoithen heautō Christou einai, touto logizesthō palin ephʼ heautou hoti kathōs autos Christou houtōs kai hēmeis.

paragraphs.text: For though I should glory somewhat abundantly concerning our authority (which the Lord gave for building you up, and not for casting you down), I shall not be put to shame:
paragraphs.original: ἐάν τε γὰρ περισσότερόν τι καυχήσωμαι περὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἡμῶν, ἧς ἔδωκεν ὁ κύριος εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν ὑμῶν, οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι,
paragraphs.translit: ean te gar perissoteron ti kauchēsōmai peri tēs exousias hēmōn, hēs edōken ho kyrios eis oikodomēn kai ouk eis kathairesin hymōn, ouk aischynthēsomai,

paragraphs.text: that I may not seem as if I would terrify you by my letters.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα μὴ δόξω ὡς ἂν ἐκφοβεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ τῶν ἐπιστολῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hina mē doxō hōs an ekphobein hymas dia tōn epistolōn·

paragraphs.text: For, His letters, they say, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι Αἱ ἐπιστολαὶ μέν, φησίν, βαρεῖαι καὶ ἰσχυραί, ἡ δὲ παρουσία τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενὴς καὶ ὁ λόγος ἐξουθενημένος.
paragraphs.translit: hoti Hai epistolai men, phēsin, bareiai kai ischyrai, hē de parousia tou sōmatos asthenēs kai ho logos exouthenēmenos.

paragraphs.text: Let such a one reckon this, that, what we are in word by letters when we are absent, such [are we] also in deed when we are present.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο λογιζέσθω ὁ τοιοῦτος, ὅτι οἷοί ἐσμεν τῷ λόγῳ διʼ ἐπιστολῶν ἀπόντες, τοιοῦτοι καὶ παρόντες τῷ ἔργῳ.
paragraphs.translit: touto logizesthō ho toioutos, hoti hoioi esmen tō logō diʼ epistolōn apontes, toioutoi kai parontes tō ergō.

paragraphs.text: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with certain of them that commend themselves: but they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ τολμῶμεν ἐγκρῖναι ἢ συγκρῖναι ἑαυτούς τισιν τῶν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστανόντων· ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἑαυτοὺς μετροῦντες καὶ συγκρίνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς οὐ συνιᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar tolmōmen enkrinai ē synkrinai heautous tisin tōn heautous synistanontōn· alla autoi en heautois heautous metrountes kai synkrinontes heautous heautois ou syniasin.

paragraphs.text: But we will not glory beyond [our] measure, but according to the measure of the province which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even unto you.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχησόμεθα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τοῦ κανόνος οὗ ἐμέρισεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεὸς μέτρου, ἐφικέσθαι ἄχρι καὶ ὑμῶν—
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de ouk eis ta ametra kauchēsometha, alla kata to metron tou kanonos hou emerisen hēmin ho theos metrou, ephikesthai achri kai hymōn—

paragraphs.text: For we stretch not ourselves overmuch, as though we reached not unto you: for we came even as far as unto you in the gospel of Christ:
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ὡς μὴ ἐφικνούμενοι εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπερεκτείνομεν ἑαυτούς, ἄχρι γὰρ καὶ ὑμῶν ἐφθάσαμεν ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ—
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hōs mē ephiknoumenoi eis hymas hyperekteinomen heautous, achri gar kai hymōn ephthasamen en tō euangeliō tou Christou—

paragraphs.text: not glorying beyond [our] measure, [that is,] in other men`s labors; but having hope that, as your faith groweth, we shall be magnified in you according to our province unto [further] abundance,
paragraphs.original: οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχώμενοι ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις κόποις, ἐλπίδα δὲ ἔχοντες αὐξανομένης τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν μεγαλυνθῆναι κατὰ τὸν κανόνα ἡμῶν εἰς περισσείαν,
paragraphs.translit: ouk eis ta ametra kauchōmenoi en allotriois kopois, elpida de echontes auxanomenēs tēs pisteōs hymōn en hymin megalynthēnai kata ton kanona hēmōn eis perisseian,

paragraphs.text: so as to preach the gospel even unto the parts beyond you, [and] not to glory in another`s province in regard of things ready to our hand.
paragraphs.original: εἰς τὰ ὑπερέκεινα ὑμῶν εὐαγγελίσασθαι, οὐκ ἐν ἀλλοτρίῳ κανόνι εἰς τὰ ἕτοιμα καυχήσασθαι.
paragraphs.translit: eis ta hyperekeina hymōn euangelisasthai, ouk en allotriō kanoni eis ta hetoima kauchēsasthai.

paragraphs.text: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ καυχώμενος ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω·
paragraphs.translit: Ho de kauchōmenos en kyriō kauchasthō·

paragraphs.text: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἑαυτὸν συνιστάνων, ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν δόκιμος, ἀλλὰ ὃν ὁ κύριος συνίστησιν.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar ho heauton synistanōn, ekeinos estin dokimos, alla hon ho kyrios synistēsin.
